senses.gloss: f. (preced. wds.) writ, deed, esp. marriage contract, containing, among other things, the settlement of a certain amount due do the wife on her husband’s death or on being divorced; K’thubah, the wife’s settlement, widowhood. [For the formula of the marriage contract, v.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 4:7-12">Keth. IV, 7—12</cite>.] <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 15:3:4">Y. Yeb. XV, 14ᵈ</cite> <he>ב״ש עבדי כ׳ מדרש</he> the Shammaites made the wording of the marriage contract the text for legal interpretation; <he>מספר כְּתוּבָּתָהּ נלמוד וכ׳</he> from her marriage contract we learn (that she must receive her widowhood), for he writes to her &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 15:3:4">Ib.</cite> <he>ר׳ מאיר עבד כ׳ וכ׳</he> R. M. made the formula of the deed of sale the text &c. (v.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 1:2">Keth. I, 2</cite> <he>בתולה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ מאתים</he> the widowhood of one marrying as a virgin is two hundred Zuz.

<cite ref="Shabbat 14b:5">Sabb. 14ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 16b:2">16ᵇ</cite> <he>שמעין</he> … <he>תיקן כ׳ לאשה</he> Simon b. Shetaḥ introduced the written marriage contract (with the promise of a widowhood, in place of a deposit of the widowhood in securities); <cite ref="Ketubot 82b:10">Keth. 82ᵇ</cite> <he>תיקן כל נכסיו אחראין לכתובתה</he> ordained that the contract must contain a clause making all his landed estate a mortgage for her widowhood; Y. ib. VIII, 32ᵇ, sq. Bab.
<cite ref="Ketubot 10a:3">ib. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>כְּתוּבַּת אשה מן התורה</he> the widowhood endowment is intimated in the Torah.
<cite ref="Ketubot 10a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>כתובת אלמנה אינה וכ׳</he> the endowment of one that married as a widow is not Biblical.
<cite ref="Ketubot 56a:17">Ib. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>כ׳ דרבנן</he> the widowhood is a Rabbinical institution.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 4:2">Ib. IV, 2</cite> <he>כְּתוּבָּתָהּ שלו</he> her widowhood belongs to him (her father).
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 9:8">Ib. IX, 8</cite> <he>הפוגמת כתובתה</he>, v. <cite ref="Q00074"><he>פָּגַם</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 9:9">Ib. 9</cite> … <he>הוציאה גט גובה כתובתה</he> if she produces evidence of divorce but has no contract to show, she is entitled to her settlement; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>כְּתוּבּוֹת</he>.

Ib. שני … כ׳ גובה שתי כ׳ if she produces two letters of divorce (evidence of having been divorced and remarried to her former husband and again divorced) and two contracts, she is entitled to two widowhoods; a. fr.—כְּתוּבּוֹת K’thuboth, name of a treatise of Mishnah, Tosefta, Talmud Babli and Y’rushalmi, of the Order of Nashim.
